column1: # CLAIMS.tsv -- the numbers this repo's documentation states, and the command
# that printed each. See tools/claimcheck.py; run it with `bash test/claims.sh`.
# Three repos in this toolchain were caught in two days publishing a score no
# gate had ever printed: the docs site's "498/498 byte-exact modules" for aowlsem
# (an hconv-site census, `oracle 527 | ours 498`, reworded into a module count --
# the real figure was 46/55), aowlc's "73/73" for a script that printed 66/67,
# and its "77/77" for one that prints 78/78. Nothing caught any of them, because
# no gate read prose.
# THIS REPO'S STRUCTURAL RISK, which is worth stating because it decides what
# this file can do: not one of aowlmony's seven test entry points has a declared
# denominator. test/test.js prints `${pass}/${pass+fail} passed` and the six
# shell scripts print `$pass passed · $fail failed` -- every total is DERIVED, so
# a check that stops running shrinks the gate silently instead of failing it.
# That is the same defect aowli's gatelib.sh was written to prevent. Until a
# declared plan exists here, a numerator from these scripts cannot be pinned by
# anything, which is why DESIGN.md's "Suite 24/25 -> 25/25" is filed as the
# record of one change rather than as a claim about the suite.
# NOT SWEPT, deliberately: DIFFERENTIATION.md and ROADMAP.md. They are strategy
# documents and say so; TOWER.md's own header calls it "a design proposal ... Not
# a description of existing code". "~80% built" and "~60% of the way to a CAS" are
# author's judgements, visibly hedged, and reading them as gate scores would be a
# category error in the other direction. What IS rowed from TOWER.md is 310/310,
# because that one is a real gate's output -- aowlparser's -- restated here where
# nothing measures it, so it is checked against aowlparser's own stress.sh.
# Columns: FILE <TAB> ANCHOR <TAB> CLASS <TAB> NUMBER <TAB> SOURCE <TAB> EXTRACT <TAB> GUARD
DESIGN.md
